overview: A one-page Department of State file-control or cross-reference sheet indexes five communications concerning the finances of the Kwantung Leased Territory. Most entries concern budgets of the territorial government or Kwantung Bureau, including a supplemental budget for 1933–34 and the budget for the fiscal year ending January 31, 1939; the final entry points to a separate file containing a report on Manchuria’s balance of international payments. The indexed communications originated principally in Dairen, with one from Mukden, and were associated with U.S. officials Vincent, Ballantine, and Turner.

subfiles.title: Index sheet for Kwantung Leased Territory financial records
subfiles.from: U.S. Department of State filing staff
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes five communications on Kwantung budgets and Manchurian financial conditions and supplies a cross-reference to another decimal-file item.
subfiles.summary: Entries 11 and 12 refer to communications from Dairen associated with Vincent concerning the Kwantung Government’s supplemental budget for 1933–34 and a copy of despatch no. 125. Entry 13 records a Mukden despatch associated with Ballantine transmitting the Kwantung Bureau budget for the fiscal year ending January 31, 1939, while entry 14 records an otherwise undescribed Dairen communication associated with Turner. Entry 15 notes Dairen despatch no. 55, also associated with Turner, reporting a schedule obtained from official sources in Hsinking on Manchuria’s balance of international payments, including the Kwantung Leased Territory, and directs the reader to file 893.51 Manchuria/97.

interest: This sheet is useful as a compact archival roadmap to several financial reports that may now be dispersed or missing from the bundle. It links territorial budget administration to the wider balance of payments of Japanese-controlled Manchuria and identifies the diplomatic posts and officers involved. The juxtaposition of 1933–34 budget material with a budget ending in 1939 also suggests that the subject file accumulated records over several years, despite incomplete and inconsistent dates in the index.
